title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:cA22}
    The PCA ${\mathcal A}(2,2)$ has dimension $l = 10$. A complete set of representatives is
    \begin{equation}
        \begin{aligned}
            &g_1 = (1)(2)(3)(4),\,
            &&g_2 = (1)(2)(34), \, 
            &&g_3 = (12)(3)(4), \,
            &&g_4 = (13)(2)(4), \,
            &&g_5 = (1)(234),   \,  \\
            &g_6 = (4)(123),    \,
            &&g_7 = (12)(34),   \,
            &&g_8 = (13)(24),   \,
            &&g_9 = (1234),     \,
            &&g_{10} = (1324)\, .
        \end{aligned}
    \end{equation}
    The choice of representatives is not unique, but the corresponding orbit sums are independent of the choice.

title: Definition
body_md:
The symbol $R \vdash L$ denotes an integer partition $R$ of $L$, or equivalently a Young diagram $R$ with $L$ boxes. The height of $R$ is the number of non-zero entries of $R$ denoted by $\ell(R)$. 
For example, the three integer partitions of $L=3$ have heights
\begin{equation}
\ell([3]) = 1, \qquad
\ell([2,1]) = 2, \qquad
\ell([1,1,1]) = 3.
\end{equation}

title: Example
body_md:
The relevant orbits for ${\mathcal A}(L,0)$ are $S_L$-orbits of $S_L$, or equivalently, conjugacy classes of $S_L$.
    Therefore, the centre has an orbit basis labelled by conjugacy classes. For $L=3$ the orbit basis is given by
    \begin{equation}
        P_{L,0}(\mathrm{id}) \propto \mathrm{id}, \quad 
        P_{L,0}((12)) \propto (12) + (13) + (23), \quad 
        P_{L,0}((123)) \propto (123) + (132) \; .
    \end{equation}

title: Remark
body_md:
\label{remark: multiplicity}
It is often useful to further refine/resolve the multiplicity label $a$ using operators that commute with the left action of the centre.
For example, one resolution involves picking out fixed irreducible representations $\Lambda$ of the $U(2)$ symmetry rotating $Z$ and $W$, which is a global symmetry of four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM.
We will come back to this point at the end of this Subsection.

title: Definition
body_md:
The adjoint action of $\omega \in \mathcal{Z}(\mathbb{C}[S_{m+n}])$ on $\sigma \in {\mathcal A}(m,n)$ is given by
    \begin{equation}
m^{\mathfrak{ad}}: \mathcal{Z}(\mathbb{C}[S_{m+n}]) \otimes {\mathcal A}(m,n) \rightarrow {\mathcal A}(m,n) , \qquad
m^{\mathfrak{ad}}[\omega](\sigma) = \sum_{g \in S_{m+n}} c_g(\omega) \, g \sigma g^{-1}.
    \end{equation}
For ${\mathcal S}(\omega)=\omega$, the adjoint action is self-adjoint with respect to the orbit-basis inner product and commutes with the left action of the centre. 
The simultaneous eigenbases are labelled by $R \vdash (m+n)$ and $\Lambda \vdash (m+n)$ with $\ell(\Lambda) \leq 2$.
The partition $\Lambda = [\lambda_1,\lambda_2]$ labels an irreducible representation of $U(2)$.
Its restriction to $SU(2)$ has spin $(\lambda_1-\lambda_2)/2$, and its total $U(1)$ degree is $\lambda_1+\lambda_2$\,.

title: Remark
body_md:
In the orbit basis, the one-loop permutation dilatation operator has rational entries.
SEP bases have integer vector solutions \cite{Padellaro:2024rld} and therefore the one-loop dilatation operator in a SEP basis has rational coefficients as well.
It follows that both factors are polynomials with rational coefficients.

name: Derangements

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $g_1,\dots,g_{r} \in D_{m+n}$ be a complete set of representatives of orbits of $S_m \times S_n$ acting on $D_{m+n}$ by conjugation.
    Since cycle structure is preserved by conjugation, every element in the orbit of a derangement is a derangement.
    The representatives label an orbit basis for the \emph{derangement orbit space} (DOS)
\begin{equation}
{\mathcal D}(m,n) = \operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb{C}}( P_{m,n}(g_p) \, \vert\, 1 \leq p \leq r  ) = {\mathcal A}(m,n) \cap \mathbb{C}[D_{m+n}] \,.
\end{equation}
Here $\mathbb{C}[D_{m+n}]$ denotes the vector subspace of $\mathbb{C}[S_{m+n}]$ spanned by $D_{m+n}$, and the inclusion $D_{m+n} \hookrightarrow S_{m+n}$ induces the natural embedding ${\mathcal D}(m,n) \hookrightarrow {\mathcal A}(m,n)$.
